items.headline: HDB launches 6,952 BTO flats across seven projects in June exercise
items.summary: The Housing Board launched 6,952 Build-To-Order flats for sale on June 17 across seven projects in towns including Ang Mo Kio, Bishan, Bukit Merah, Sembawang and Woodlands; a Bishan project brings public housing to Upper Thomson for the first time, with applications to June 24.

items.headline: Singapore's non-oil exports jump 38.4% in May on AI-driven electronics demand
items.summary: Non-oil domestic exports rose 38.4% year on year in May, the fastest pace since December 2003, Enterprise Singapore data showed on June 17; electronics shipments surged 94.8%, led by integrated circuits, PCs and disk media amid the global AI build-out.

items.headline: MAS survey trims Singapore's 2026 growth forecast to 3.5% on geopolitical risk
items.summary: The MAS quarterly Survey of Professional Forecasters, released June 17, cut the median 2026 GDP growth forecast to 3.5% from 3.6%, citing Middle East conflict as the main downside risk; most economists expect monetary policy to stay unchanged in July.

items.headline: CNA tops Reuters Institute 2026 rankings for Singapore online news use
items.summary: The Reuters Institute Digital News Report 2026 ranked CNA the most-used online news source in Singapore at 47% weekly reach, ahead of Mothership and The Straits Times; trust in news in Singapore stood at 46%, above the global average of 37%.

items.headline: Car and taxi collide outside Bendemeer MRT, driver flees as cabby hospitalised
items.summary: A rental car and a taxi collided near Bendemeer MRT station along Kallang Bahru on the morning of June 17, knocking down a stretch of central-divider railing and deploying both vehicles' airbags; the taxi driver was hospitalised while the car driver fled.

items.headline: NSE files for India's largest-ever IPO with up to 148.9 million shares on offer
items.summary: The National Stock Exchange filed draft papers with SEBI on June 17 for what is set to be India's biggest IPO, an all offer-for-sale of up to 148.9 million shares (about a 5% stake); sellers are eyeing roughly 20,000-25,000 crore rupees at a valuation near 5 lakh crore rupees.

items.headline: Delhi Police bust ISI-backed terror module linked to D-Company, seven arrested
items.summary: Delhi Police's Special Cell said on June 16 it had dismantled a Pakistan ISI-backed terror-crime syndicate tied to Dawood Ibrahim's D-Company, arresting seven men and seizing five pistols; investigators said the network had scouted targets in Delhi and Mumbai.

items.headline: India blocks Telegram until June 22 and curbs message editing before NEET re-exam
items.summary: The IT ministry restricted access to Telegram in India from June 16 to 22 under Section 69A and ordered the app to disable message editing until June 30, acting on the National Testing Agency's advice to curb cheating before the NEET-UG re-examination on June 21.

items.headline: Nifty tops 24,000 as Indian shares rise a fourth day before the Fed decision
items.summary: The Nifty 50 closed above 24,000 and the Sensex added 347 points on June 17, a fourth straight gain, as easing oil prices lifted sentiment before the US Federal Reserve's decision; mid- and small-cap stocks outperformed the main indices.

items.headline: G7 closes Evian summit with pledge to boost Ukraine air defences and Russia sanctions
items.summary: G7 leaders ended their summit in Evian, France on June 17 vowing unwavering support for Ukraine, agreeing to send more air-defence systems and interceptors and to tighten sanctions on Russia's oil and gas sectors; they said Russia had shown no serious willingness to make peace.

items.headline: Update: US-Iran accord set to be signed June 19 with Hormuz toll-free for 60 days
items.summary: The United States and Iran are due to formally sign their war-ending accord on June 19 in Switzerland, after a memorandum approved electronically set the Strait of Hormuz to stay toll-free for 60 days; sanctioned Iranian tankers resumed sailing through the strait past the lifted US blockade.

items.headline: Messi hat-trick equals Klose's World Cup goal record as Argentina beat Algeria 3-0
items.summary: Lionel Messi, 38, scored his first World Cup hat-trick to reach 16 goals at the tournament, equalling Miroslav Klose's all-time record, as holders Argentina beat Algeria 3-0 on June 17; he became the oldest player to score a hat-trick at a World Cup.

items.headline: England beat Croatia 4-2 in their World Cup opener as Kane scores twice
items.summary: Harry Kane scored twice and Jude Bellingham and Marcus Rashford added second-half goals as England beat Croatia 4-2 in their World Cup Group L opener in Dallas on June 17; the first half had ended 2-2 before England pulled clear.

items.headline: SpaceX to buy AI coding startup Cursor for $60 billion days after its IPO
items.summary: SpaceX agreed on June 16 to acquire Anysphere, the maker of the AI coding tool Cursor, in an all-stock deal valuing it at $60 billion, days after its record Nasdaq debut; the takeover, expected to close in the third quarter, strengthens Elon Musk's xAI in AI coding.

items.headline: Snap unveils $2,195 Specs augmented-reality glasses as shares slide
items.summary: Snap opened preorders on June 16 for its consumer AR glasses, Specs, priced at $2,195 with a $200 refundable deposit and shipping in the autumn in the US, UK and France; the high price drew criticism and Snap's shares fell.

items.headline: World-model startup Odyssey raises $310 million at a $1.45 billion valuation
items.summary: Odyssey, founded by self-driving veterans Oliver Cameron and Jeff Hawke, raised a $310 million Series B at a $1.45 billion valuation led by Natural Capital, with Amazon, AMD Ventures and GV joining; AWS becomes its preferred cloud and it will tune its models for Amazon's Trainium chips.

items.headline: Google launches its first Gemini-built smart speaker at $99.99
items.summary: Google introduced the $99.99 Google Home Speaker on June 17, its first audio device built specifically for Gemini, swapping fixed Assistant commands for conversational, multi-step requests; a Google Home Premium tier costs $10 a month for advanced Gemini Live features.

items.headline: Anthropic becomes first standalone AI firm to join Frontier carbon-removal group
items.summary: Anthropic joined the Frontier carbon-removal coalition on June 17, contributing to a new $915 million tranche that nearly doubles the group's pledges to about $1.8 billion; it is the first pure-play AI company to join, alongside founding member Google, as scrutiny of AI energy use grows.

items.headline: Fed holds rates at 3.5-3.75% but hawkish projections signal a 2026 hike
items.summary: At Kevin Warsh's first meeting as chair, the Federal Reserve voted 12-0 on June 17 to keep its benchmark rate at 3.5% to 3.75%, a fourth straight hold; new projections showed nine of 18 officials expect at least one hike this year, and Warsh declined to submit his own dot.

items.headline: Wall Street slides as hawkish Fed hits tech; Dow falls 507 points
items.summary: US stocks fell after the Fed's hawkish projections on June 17, with the Dow dropping 507 points, or 0.98%, the S&P 500 down 1.21% and the Nasdaq off 1.34%; big-tech names including Microsoft, Meta, Alphabet and Amazon all closed lower.

items.headline: US Treasury yields jump as Fed dot plot lifts bets on a 2026 rate hike
items.summary: Treasury yields rose sharply after the Fed's projections on June 17, with the two-year yield climbing more than 16 basis points to about 4.22% as traders priced a possible rate increase as early as October; the move tracked the hawkish shift in officials' forecasts.

items.headline: Yum! Brands sells Pizza Hut for $2.7 billion in two deals
items.summary: Yum! Brands said on June 16 it would sell Pizza Hut for $2.7 billion in total, with the business outside mainland China going to private-equity firm LongRange Capital for about $1.5 billion and the China operations to Yum China for roughly $1.2 billion; Yum expects about $2.3 billion in net proceeds.

items.headline: Olin and Huntsman to merge in all-stock deal creating a $12 billion chemicals firm
items.summary: Olin and Huntsman agreed on June 16 to combine in an all-stock merger of equals to form OlinHuntsman, a North American chemicals company with about $12.5 billion in combined 2025 revenue; Huntsman holders receive 0.5476 Olin shares each, and the deal is expected to close in the first half of 2027.

items.headline: India crush Afghanistan by 170 runs as Gill and Kishan hit centuries
items.summary: Shubman Gill made 154 and Ishan Kishan 125 as India piled up 402 and bowled Afghanistan out for 232 to win the second ODI by 170 runs in Lucknow on June 17, taking an unbeatable 2-0 series lead; their third-wicket stand was worth 224.

items.headline: India post record 209 for 5 to beat Netherlands by 95 at Women's T20 World Cup
items.summary: Smriti Mandhana hit 74 and Shafali Verma chipped in with bat and ball as India made 209 for 5, their highest Women's T20 World Cup total, then held the Netherlands to 114 to win by 95 runs at Headingley on June 17; Shree Charani took four wickets.

items.headline: Australia hold Bangladesh to 77 and win by nine wickets
items.summary: Australia restricted Bangladesh to 77 for 8, the lowest total of this Women's T20 World Cup, and knocked off the runs in 9.3 overs to win by nine wickets at Headingley on June 17; Georgia Voll finished 45 not out.

items.headline: Badosa fights back to upset Coco Gauff and reach Berlin quarterfinals
items.summary: Paula Badosa recovered from a set down to beat fifth seed Coco Gauff 1-6, 6-3, 6-2 in Berlin on June 17, reaching the grass-court quarterfinals where she will meet defending champion Jessica Pegula.

items.headline: Medvedev and Shelton advance at the Halle grass-court tournament
items.summary: Daniil Medvedev beat France's Terence Atmane and Ben Shelton saw off Lorenzo Sonego 7-5, 6-3 to progress at the Terra Wortmann Open in Halle on June 17, as the grass-court swing built towards Wimbledon.

fun_fact.headline: There are more trees on Earth than stars in the Milky Way
fun_fact.body: There are more trees on Earth than there are stars in the Milky Way. A landmark 2015 global census published in the journal Nature put the planet's tree count at roughly 3 trillion, while NASA estimates the Milky Way holds about 100 to 400 billion stars. That makes trees outnumber our galaxy's stars by something like ten to one.

puzzle.title: The Two-Egg Drop
puzzle.body: A building has 100 floors. You have two identical glass eggs. There is some floor N such that an egg dropped from floor N or higher breaks, while an egg dropped from any floor below N survives and can be reused. An egg that breaks is gone for good. Using the strategy that minimises the number of drops needed in the worst case, how many drops do you need to be certain of finding N?
puzzle.approach: Plan the first egg's jumps so that the worst case always costs the same number of drops.
puzzle.answer: 14. Drop the first egg from floor 14; if it survives, go up 13 to floor 27, then 12 to 39, then 11, and so on with shrinking jumps. When the first egg breaks, walk the second egg up one floor at a time through the small gap below. The worst case always totals 14, because 14 + 13 + ... + 1 = 105 floors covers all 100, and 13 (covering only 91) is not enough.
